joti.tagline: A space for each part of your day.
joti.summary: Joti is a web application in development that brings documents, notes, lists, a calendar and a gallery into configurable private spaces.
joti.problem: Ideas, documents and tasks for the same project often end up scattered across tools. Joti aims to keep that context together and let each space show only the modules it needs.
objectives: Organize content in spaces with tools that can be enabled and disabled.
Connect quick idea capture with documents and structured lists.
Preserve drafts and detect conflicts to protect work during editing.
joti.solution: I am developing a modular application with shared navigation across its tools. Each space retains its content and settings; disabling a module hides it without deleting its records. The current version supports private spaces with a single owner.

highlights.title: Configurable spaces
highlights.text: Persistent names, icons, colors, favorites and ordering. Each space lets you choose its tools and re-enable them while retaining content.

highlights.title: Pages and notes
highlights.text: Visual and Markdown editing with autosave and draft recovery. Notes add quick capture, tags, history and conversion to independent pages.

highlights.title: Structured lists
highlights.text: Tables with typed properties, views, filters and sorting. They support CSV import and export, row reordering and keyboard cell editing.

highlights.title: Calendar
highlights.text: Month, week and day views with search and filters. All-day events are handled separately from timed events with a timezone.

highlights.title: Private gallery
highlights.text: Images organized into albums and tags, with multiple views and an expandable viewer. Originals are preserved while optimized versions support browsing.

technicalDecisions.title: Modules on a shared foundation
technicalDecisions.text: Next.js and TypeScript organize the app by feature. A pnpm and Turborepo monorepo shares components and configuration between the web application and documentation.

technicalDecisions.title: Reactive data and permissions
technicalDecisions.text: Convex handles data and subscriptions. Sessions use HttpOnly cookies, and the backend checks the session and space ownership for each protected operation.

technicalDecisions.title: Editing with recovery
technicalDecisions.text: Local drafts help recover unsaved changes. Revisions detect stale writes, while operation identifiers prevent duplicate operations on retries.

technicalDecisions.title: Separate content and media
technicalDecisions.text: Tiptap edits documents stored as Markdown. The gallery preserves originals in Convex Storage and uses Sharp to generate WebP derivatives with private access.

future: Prepare the first public deployment and complete flow validation.
Extend the permission model to introduce collaboration between users.
joti.galleryIntro: Cropped tool screenshots from development, with sample data. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.
joti.results: Joti remains in development and has no public demo yet. The repository includes the tools described here and automated tests for its modules. Current spaces are private; shared permissions and simultaneous collaborative editing are not implemented yet.

gitpilot.tagline: Git identities for personal and work projects.
gitpilot.summary: GitPilot organizes author profiles and applies identity rules by folder or repository on Windows and Linux. Compare your intended identity with the values Git will use for your next commit.
gitpilot.problem: Switching between personal and work projects means checking which name and email Git will use. A global setting or local override can assign a commit to the wrong identity.
gitpilot.solution: I built a local inventory that links directories and repositories to author profiles. GitPilot queries the Git CLI for effective values and previews changes before applying them.

highlights.title: Profiles and inventory
highlights.text: Save profiles, scan directories, exclude paths, and set repository overrides.

highlights.title: Review and recovery
highlights.text: Review the scope of configuration changes before confirming. GitPilot saves an encrypted backup and logs operations so you can restore them from Activity.

highlights.title: Portability
highlights.text: Export profiles, assignments, and preferences to JSON. Review the proposed changes before saving an import.

highlights.title: Inspector and GitHub
highlights.text: Check identity, signing, and remote access separately. Link a local repository to an authorized GitHub remote.

technicalDecisions.title: Git CLI as the source of truth
technicalDecisions.text: The diagnosis queries Git for effective values. Rust controls file access and configuration operations.

technicalDecisions.title: Local data and separate credentials
technicalDecisions.text: SQLite stores profiles and inventory. Credentials are stored in Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service.

gitpilot.galleryIntro: Actual screenshots of GitPilot v1.0.0 with sample data. Select an image to enlarge it.
gitpilot.results: GitPilot v1.0.0 is available on GitHub Releases as a Windows x64 installer and a Debian amd64 package. An OpenPGP-signed SHA-256 manifest accompanies the distribution files.

fym.tagline: From browsing to your next movie.
fym.summary: FyM (Find Your Movie) is a web application for exploring movies and TV shows, discovering cast members, browsing scenes and watching trailers.
fym.problem: Exploring a movie also means discovering its cast, watching a trailer and finding related titles. FyM brings this information into a browsing experience dedicated to movies and TV shows.
objectives: Explore movies and shows in a catalog.
Read details and discover audiovisual content.
Find content through search and filters.
fym.solution: A web application built with Next.js and React, using TMDB as its information source. Catalog browsing connects to dedicated detail pages for movies and TV shows.

highlights.title: Explore the catalog
highlights.text: Movies and TV shows with information to help discover what to watch.

highlights.title: Search and filter
highlights.text: Content search, genre filters and sorting options.

highlights.title: Discover the story
highlights.text: Detail pages with cast members, trailers and more information about each title.

technicalDecisions.title: Hybrid rendering
technicalDecisions.text: The README documents server-side data loading and client components for filters and interaction.

technicalDecisions.title: Debounced search
technicalDecisions.text: Search waits for a pause in typing to avoid making a request on every keystroke.

fym.results: The portfolio catalog lists FyM as in production. The application and source code are available through this case study’s links.

meetmesh.summary: A web application for creating and joining virtual meetings, sharing your screen and personalizing profiles.
meetmesh.problem: A virtual meeting needs to bring participants together and let them share what they are seeing. MeetMesh addresses that flow from creating a room to communicating inside it.
meetmesh.solution: A meeting application with a Next.js and React interface. It combines WebRTC, Socket.IO and Supabase for communication, room coordination and user accounts.

highlights.title: Meeting rooms
highlights.text: Create rooms and join using a room code.

highlights.title: Screen sharing
highlights.text: Share visual content during the call.

highlights.title: Personal profiles
highlights.text: Customize your name, username and avatar.

technicalDecisions.title: Browser-to-browser media
technicalDecisions.text: WebRTC carries audio and video between peers. A separate Socket.IO server exchanges signaling messages.

technicalDecisions.title: Identity and profiles
technicalDecisions.text: Supabase provides authentication and storage for profiles.

meetmesh.results: MeetMesh is listed as in development in the portfolio. A repository and web demo are available; calls also depend on the signaling service.

biovision-suite.summary: A desktop application for facial biometric analysis, enrollment, identity comparison and search, with local processing and privacy.
biovision-suite.problem: Biometric analysis handles sensitive information. BioVision Suite focuses on performing facial processing and storage on the device, without depending on a cloud API to operate.
objectives: Enroll people with image quality checks.
Compare faces and search for matches.
Analyze images, cameras and video locally.
biovision-suite.solution: A Python and PySide6 desktop suite combining computer vision, ONNX Runtime inference, FAISS vector search, and persistence with SQLite and SQLAlchemy.

highlights.title: Enrollment
highlights.text: Register people with image quality validation.

highlights.title: 1:N search
highlights.text: Find matches within the collection using FAISS.

highlights.title: Camera and video
highlights.text: Facial recognition and video file analysis.

technicalDecisions.title: Separate layers
technicalDecisions.text: The PySide6 interface is separated from services, vision engines and persistence repositories.

technicalDecisions.title: Local operation
technicalDecisions.text: Models are downloaded on the first run. Afterwards, inference and storage operate on the device.

biovision-suite.results: BioVision Suite is listed as in development. Its repository documents installation and use; as a desktop application, it has no web demo.
